title: Myasthenic crisis
subject: neurology
summary: Myasthenic weakness threatening breathing or swallowing: monitor FVC and NIF serially in ICU, give plasma exchange or IVIg 2 g/kg, treat the trigger, stop drugs that worsen myasthenia, and hold pyridostigmine once intubated.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Myasthenic crisis (MGFA class V): worsening weakness needing intubation, or NIV to avoid intubation. Impending crisis: rapid worsening that could lead to crisis within days to weeks.
Warning signs: dysphagia, nasal speech, weak cough, neck flexor weakness, orthopnoea, paradoxical breathing, inability to count to 20 in one breath, pooling of secretions.

Triggers: infection (most common), surgery including thymectomy, pregnancy and postpartum, starting high-dose corticosteroids, tapering immunosuppression, drugs that worsen myasthenia, thyroid disease, immune checkpoint inhibitors.
Cholinergic crisis from excess pyridostigmine is now rare: suspect with miosis, heavy secretions, bradycardia, fasciculations, cramps and diarrhoea.

sections.title: Airway and breathing
items: Admit impending crisis to a monitored bed with ICU access; manifest crisis to ICU.
Measure FVC and negative inspiratory force (NIF) at least every 4 hours while worsening, with single breath count, cough and swallow. SpO2 and blood gases change late.
20/30/40 rule: FVC below 20 mL/kg, NIF weaker than minus 30 cmH2O or maximum expiratory pressure below 40 cmH2O means high risk; prepare for ventilatory support.
Intubate for FVC around 15 mL/kg or less, rising PaCO2, fatigue, or inability to clear secretions or protect the airway; do not wait for hypoxaemia.
Early BiPAP may avoid intubation in selected patients, ideally before hypercapnia develops and when secretions and bulbar function allow.
Intubation drugs (anaesthetist-led): myasthenic patients are resistant to suxamethonium and very sensitive to non-depolarising blockers; use reduced doses and neuromuscular monitoring.
Hold pyridostigmine once intubated (it increases airway secretions and confuses assessment of weakness); restart at a low dose, for example 30 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours, before extubation.

sections.title: Rescue immunotherapy
items: Plasma exchange (PLEX) or IVIg is first-line. Trials show similar efficacy; experts regard PLEX as faster and more effective in crisis, and it may be better in MuSK-positive myasthenia.
PLEX: 5 exchanges of 1 to 1.5 plasma volumes on alternate days (about 10 days). Avoid in sepsis or haemodynamic instability.
IVIg: 2 g/kg total over 2 to 5 days (0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days or 1 g/kg/day for 2 days). Avoid in renal failure; caution with thrombotic risk; hydrate.

Corticosteroids are started or increased with neurology, usually alongside PLEX or IVIg. Because they can cause transient worsening in the first 2 weeks, it may be appropriate to wait several days for PLEX or IVIg to take effect first.

Refractory disease: neurology may add FcRn inhibitors (efgartigimod, rozanolixizumab) or complement inhibitors (eculizumab, ravulizumab, zilucoplan), which require meningococcal vaccination or antibiotic prophylaxis.
Treat the trigger: culture and treat infection promptly, preferring beta-lactams over fluoroquinolones, macrolides and aminoglycosides.

sections.title: Drugs to avoid or use with caution (MGFA 2020)
items: Avoid: telithromycin, botulinum toxin, D-penicillamine. IV magnesium only if absolutely necessary (for example eclampsia) with close observation.

Use cautiously, if at all, and observe for worsening: fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, beta-blockers, procainamide, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine, quinine (only for malaria), statins, desferrioxamine, iodinated contrast, immune checkpoint inhibitors.
Corticosteroids may cause transient worsening within the first 2 weeks. Live vaccines are contraindicated in patients on immunosuppressants.

Pregnancy: oral pyridostigmine is first-line and IV cholinesterase inhibitors can cause uterine contractions. Prednisolone is the immunosuppressant of choice; mycophenolate and methotrexate are contraindicated.
Eclampsia in myasthenia: avoid magnesium sulfate (barbiturates or phenytoin usually suffice). Examine every newborn for transient neonatal myasthenia.

sections.title: Monitoring and weaning
items: Serial FVC, NIF, swallow and neck flexion power; cardiac monitoring; correct potassium, magnesium, phosphate and calcium, as low levels worsen weakness.
PLEX: watch for line infection, thrombosis, hypotension and citrate-related hypocalcaemia. IVIg: renal function, headache, thrombosis.
Nasogastric feeding if bulbar weakness; aspiration precautions; VTE prophylaxis.
Extubate only when FVC, NIF, cough and bulbar function have clearly improved; reintubation is common, so wean gradually and consider BiPAP after extubation.

sections.title: After the crisis
items: Arrange CT chest for thymoma if not done and plan thymectomy with neurology once stable.
Plan long-term immunosuppression and give the patient a written list of drugs to avoid.
Before discharge, confirm stable breathing and swallowing, a clear steroid and immunosuppressant plan with bone and gastric protection, and early neurology follow-up.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for hypoxaemia or hypercapnia before escalating care.
Increasing pyridostigmine for worsening weakness in crisis (more secretions, risk of cholinergic weakness).
Starting high-dose steroids alone in an unmonitored patient with bulbar or respiratory weakness.
Treating the precipitating chest infection with a fluoroquinolone or macrolide.
Missing myasthenia as the cause of unexplained respiratory failure or failed extubation after surgery.

drugs.name: Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg)
drugs.dose: 2 g/kg IV total over 2 to 5 days (0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days or 1 g/kg/day for 2 days)
drugs.notes: Avoid in renal failure; caution with thrombotic risk.

drugs.name: Plasma exchange (PLEX)
drugs.dose: 5 exchanges of 1 to 1.5 plasma volumes on alternate days
drugs.notes: Faster onset; preferred in MuSK-positive disease. Avoid in sepsis or shock.

drugs.name: Pyridostigmine
drugs.dose: Restart at 30 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours before extubation, then titrate
drugs.notes: Hold while intubated. Excess causes secretions and cholinergic weakness.
